$comment: The one source of truth for what the workflow studio offers and what the engine will run (#107). The SPA imports this file for the BPMN types reference panel; AutoNate.Web embeds these same bytes and refuses a deployment containing anything the engine cannot execute. Keyed on (localName, eventDefinition) because a localName-only key cannot tell the eight boundary variants apart, and seven of them execute.

studio.$doc: What the studio advertises. Drives the BPMN types panel and nothing else.
studio.supported: Authorable in the studio today. For an executable element that means configurable and running; for an annotation it means drawable, which is all one can be.
studio.coming-soon: Offered by BPMN and runnable by the engine, but Auton8 has not wired the authoring side yet. An M4/M5 story owns it.
studio.withdrawn: Will not be built. Not advertised anywhere.

engine.$doc: What Flowable actually does with it, established by deploying it (#103). Drives publish validation and nothing else.
engine.annotation: Deploys and carries no execution semantics BY DESIGN — a BPMN artifact, not a gap. Never refused.
engine.cannot-execute: Deploys into silence, or is rejected by the engine. Refused at publish, quoting `reason`.

$fields.$invariant: studio=supported implies engine is not cannot-execute. The studio may not claim support for something the engine will not run; BpmnSupportManifestTests enforces it.

generatedFrom: #103 inventory — every verdict produced by deploying to a running engine

elements.name: Task (Generic)
elements.reason: A plain bpmn:task is the same silent pass-through as a manual task. The studio converts it to a user task at design time (#167).
elements.evidence: deployed and started, then re-probed for #167 and observed NOT to wait. The earlier 'deployed and started' verdict was true and misleading

elements.name: Message Start Event
elements.reason: #340: the studio cannot name the message. `updateMessageElementProperties` (workflow.js) writes only autonateCorrelationKey / autonateTargetProcessKey / autonateMessageName -- never messageRef -- and nothing in the SPA creates a <bpmn:message> root; contrast ensureSignalRootElement, which exists for signals. WorkflowStudio.tsx gates the Message field on selection.type === 'bpmn:SendTask' and renders it disabled otherwise. So a message event placed from the palette has no messageRef, cannot be given one, and publish refuses it with a remedy the product does not offer. The ENGINE axis is untouched: Flowable runs a correctly configured message event, and message correlation works -- every E2E test seeds its <bpmn:message> roots through the API, so Outcome 4 is unaffected. What was false was the authorability claim, exactly as it was for Send Task in #316. Making these authorable is M4b.

elements.name: Conditional Start Event
elements.reason: #162: triggers when its condition becomes true, inside an event subprocess -- the only place Flowable allows one, which is why #158 could refuse the process-level placement but not deliver the working one. Reuses #158 evaluate-conditions trigger.
elements.evidence: legal only inside an event subprocess, not at process level

elements.name: Error Start Event
elements.reason: #162: catches an error raised anywhere in the containing scope, including from a nested subprocess. A non-interrupting error start is refused: BPMN forbids it and the engine interrupts regardless, so the diagram would promise something it does not do.

elements.name: Escalation Start Event
elements.reason: #162: catches an escalation raised in the containing scope, and a non-interrupting one lets that scope carry on -- asserted in its own right rather than by analogy with error.

elements.name: Compensation Start Event
elements.reason: Flowable 8.0.0 has no EventSubProcessCompensationStartEventActivityBehavior. Descoped 2026-09-07 (#115).

elements.name: Intermediate Throw (None)
elements.evidence: deployed and executed: the token passes straight through, which is the whole behaviour (#167)

elements.name: Intermediate Throw (Signal)
elements.reason: #156: raises a signal and execution continues past it. Unlike its message counterpart, Flowable executes this as authored.

elements.name: Intermediate Throw (Escalation)
elements.reason: #114: raises its code and execution continues past it, which is what distinguishes escalation from error.

elements.name: Intermediate Throw (Link)
elements.reason: Flowable 8.0.0 has no link event type in its BPMN model at all, so the XML converter discards it before validation and the jump silently does not exist. Descoped by spike #217. Use a sequence flow instead — BPMN defines link events as a drawing convenience, and they add no execution semantics a sequence flow does not already have.
elements.evidence: no link type in the BPMN model at all (spike #217)

elements.name: Intermediate Throw (Compensation)
elements.reason: #115: verified against 8.0.0. Compensation runs the handlers for activities that actually completed, in REVERSE order, and the throw waits for them before the process continues — measured with a recorded trail ('h3;h1;after;'), not by reading timestamps. A handler failure propagates rather than being swallowed.
elements.evidence: deployed and started; compensation order and skipping verified

elements.name: Timer Boundary
elements.evidence: deployed and fired against a live engine (#157): interrupting cancels the attached activity, non-interrupting leaves it running, R3/PT1S fires exactly three times, and completing the activity first removes the timer job

elements.name: Signal Boundary
elements.reason: #156: interrupting and non-interrupting both verified; non-interrupting leaves the guarded activity running.

elements.name: Conditional Boundary
elements.evidence: deployed, started, and advanced by an explicit evaluate-conditions call (#158)

elements.name: Error Boundary
elements.reason: #114: catches a matching error code and interrupts the attached activity. Verified end to end — the boundary path ran and the normal path did not.

elements.name: Escalation Boundary
elements.reason: #114: interrupting and non-interrupting both verified — non-interrupting leaves the attached activity running.

elements.name: Cancel Boundary
elements.reason: #220 descoped: the BPMN rollback idiom fails at runtime on Flowable 8.0.0 -- the boundary cannot resolve the transaction execution, and one path corrupts act_ru_execution with a foreign-key violation. Engine defect, tracked in #228.
elements.evidence: BoundaryCancelEventActivityBehavior ships; minimal transaction completed before the cancel applied

elements.name: Compensation Boundary
elements.reason: #115: the boundary event plus a <association> to an activity marked isForCompensation is what Flowable runs. Only activities that completed are compensated — an activity skipped by a gateway never had its handler run. A handler that WAITS (a user task or receive task) is refused at publish: Flowable fails its own transaction with an act_fk_exe_parent violation when such a handler is compensated during a task completion, and the task can then never be completed.
elements.evidence: deployed and started; compensation order and skipping verified

elements.name: Boundary Event (None)
elements.reason: #282: a boundary event with no event definition has nothing to wait for. Flowable refuses the deployment outright — [Validation set: 'flowable-executable-process' | Problem: 'flowable-boundary-event-no-event-definition'] — so it is withdrawn from the palette and refused at publish, naming the step. It had no row at all until #282, which meant the popup filter had no deny key for it and publish had nothing to match: it was placeable, published with zero errors, and failed at the engine.
elements.evidence: deployed against a live 8.0.0 engine and refused: flowable-boundary-event-no-event-definition

elements.name: Signal End
elements.reason: #156: on its own this deploys, ends the process, and RAISES NOTHING -- verified, a catcher waiting on the same name sat untouched while an intermediate throw of that signal fired it instantly. Publish rewrites it into an intermediate throw plus a terminal end event, so it does what it says.

elements.name: Error End
elements.reason: #114: raises its code. An error NOTHING catches destroys the whole instance (Flowable answers the start call with 500 and leaves no history), so publish now refuses that diagram.
elements.evidence: raw probe had no catching boundary; a modelling requirement, not an engine gap

elements.name: Escalation End
elements.reason: #114: ends the subprocess raising its code, asserted directly rather than by analogy with the error end event.

elements.name: Cancel End
elements.reason: #220 descoped: raising cancel from inside a transaction fails at runtime on Flowable 8.0.0. Engine defect, tracked in #228.

elements.name: Compensation End
elements.reason: #115: executes by publish-time expansion. The raw element ends the process and compensates NOTHING — verified, the handler trail came back empty — the same silent-decoration shape as Message End (#112) and Signal End (#156). Publish rewrites the deployed copy into an intermediate throw followed by a none end event; the authored diagram keeps the end event.
elements.evidence: deployed and started; compensation order and skipping verified

elements.name: Send Task
elements.reason: #316: the studio cannot configure a deployable send task. Flowable requires 'type' or 'operation' and refuses the whole deployment otherwise (flowable-sendtask-invalid-implementation); Auton8's expansion converts one only when it carries flowable:behaviorKey='autonate.send-message', and the studio cannot write that onto a send task -- updateServiceTaskProperties throws unless the element is a bpmn:ServiceTask, and selecting a send task routes to the message editor, whose only write is the message name. So EVERY send task an author could place was undeployable while this row read studio: supported, and publish said nothing. The ENGINE axis is unchanged: Flowable runs a correctly configured send task, which is why engine stays 'executes'. Use a service task, or an intermediate throw message event.
elements.evidence: deployed against a live 8.0.0 engine in its default palette state and refused: flowable-sendtask-invalid-implementation

elements.name: Receive Task
elements.reason: #112: no message subscription, so it is addressed by element id and advanced with `trigger` rather than `messageEventReceived`. Verified.

elements.name: Manual Task
elements.reason: A manual task does not wait — the engine passes straight through it, creating no task and pausing nowhere. The studio converts it to a user task at design time (#167).
elements.evidence: deployed, started, and observed NOT to wait: the process reached the next activity immediately

elements.name: Business Rule Task
elements.reason: Requires the DMN/rules engine, which is not in the Flowable image (NoClassDefFoundError org/kie/api) — see #105.
elements.evidence: NoClassDefFoundError org/kie/api — rules engine absent from the image (#105)

elements.name: Call Activity
elements.reason: #113: the author picks a published workflow; publish resolves that key to the definition that exists then and pins the deployed copy by id, because Flowable otherwise resolves the key at run time to whatever is latest — verified, an unchanged parent picked up a child version published after it.
elements.evidence: first probe named a callee that did not exist; with a real callee, executes

elements.name: Sub-Process (Embedded)
elements.evidence: deployed and executed two levels deep (#161); variables cross the boundary in both directions, and the subprocess reports its own activity instance so the execution view shows where the process is

elements.name: Event Sub-Process
elements.reason: #162: starts on its own event rather than a sequence flow. Interrupting cancels the containing scope (asserted on the cancellation); non-interrupting runs alongside it. An event subprocess with no start event, or one starting on nothing, is refused at publish -- both deploy cleanly and never trigger.

elements.name: Transaction
elements.reason: #220 descoped: the container deploys and runs, but its distinguishing behaviour -- rollback via cancel events -- does not (#228). Offering it would be offering a subprocess under a name that promises rollback it cannot do.

elements.name: Ad-Hoc Sub-Process
elements.reason: #163: Flowable runs it and exposes NO REST surface for it. AdhocSubProcessActivityBehavior ships in 8.0.0 and RuntimeService carries the commands, but flowable-rest exposes none of them, so the extension adds actuator endpoints for listing enabled activities, starting one, and completing the subprocess. Verified: nothing auto-starts, the enabled activities come back with their names, and starting one twice produces two live instances of it — the repeatability that distinguishes this element from a parallel subprocess. Publish refuses an ad-hoc subprocess with no completion condition, which would otherwise deploy and then never finish.
elements.evidence: deployed and started; enabled activities listed and started twice

elements.name: Event-Based Gateway
elements.reason: #164: the first event to arrive takes its path and the others are cancelled — verified both ways round, with the loser asserted cancelled rather than merely not taken. Publish refuses a gateway with one path (which Flowable deploys happily) and one pointing at a receive task (which BPMN allows and this engine does not).

elements.name: Complex Gateway
elements.reason: #218: executes by publish-time expansion. Flowable has no ComplexGatewayActivityBehavior, so the element's own activation condition is never evaluated — but it is NOT inert, and #103's "passes the token straight through" understates it. Verified against 8.0.0: it is recorded as activityType exclusiveGateway, it evaluates conditionExpression on its outgoing flows, it honours `default`, and with two conditions true it takes the first match. So a hand-authored complex gateway silently picks a branch. Publish now puts an author-written routing script in front of it and conditions its routes on the result, and the script must return one of the routes it was given.
elements.evidence: deployed and started; routing verified both ways round

elements.name: Loop Marker
elements.reason: #159: it does NOTHING. Measured against a control on the same task, every spelling of standardLoopCharacteristics ran the activity once — loopCondition ${true} with loopMaximum=3, ${loopCounter < 3}, and flowable:testBefore — while multiInstanceLoopCharacteristics with cardinality 3 on that same task ran it three times. So the marker is not mis-set and the measurement is not wrong: Flowable 8.0.0 has no standard loop. #103 recorded 'executes', which is wrong. Refused at publish, pointing at multi-instance, which does what an author reaching for a loop almost always wants.
elements.evidence: deployed and started; one iteration against a three-iteration control

elements.name: Multi-Instance (Parallel)
elements.reason: #159: verified against 8.0.0. Parallel creates its instances concurrently (3 live user tasks) and sequential runs them one at a time (1 live task); each instance sees its own item through elementVariable; loopCardinality creates a fixed count; a completionCondition ends the set early and cancels the rest; and an EMPTY collection completes the activity immediately rather than hanging. Completion conditions go through the shared condition check.
elements.evidence: deployed and started; per-instance element values and live-task counts observed. #245: the cardinality, early-completion-with-cancellation, independent assignment and result-aggregation claims are asserted in MultiInstanceExecutionTests, and the stored-to-deployed rewrite in MultiInstanceExpansionTests -- they were manual probes when this row was written, and two of them named features that did not exist yet.

elements.name: Compensation Marker
elements.reason: #115: isForCompensation is what makes an activity a handler rather than a step nothing can reach. It survives the studio round trip untouched, along with the association — asserted, because bpmn-js drops what its moddle does not model.
elements.evidence: deployed and started; compensation order and skipping verified

elements.name: Data Object Reference
elements.reason: #166: a declaration that executes. Verified against 8.0.0 — a <dataObject> creates a real process variable with its declared type (amount = 42.5, type=double) and a gateway condition reads it. Stored as autonate:dataType and rewritten at publish into itemSubjectRef, because NEITHER BPMN spelling does both jobs: the bare QName types the variable but bpmn-js drops it (moddle resolves itemSubjectRef as a reference and a bare QName names nothing), while an itemDefinition indirection survives the modeller and leaves the engine producing string for everything. The declared type is NOT enforced at run time — assigning a string to an xsd:double variable replaces both value and type silently — so the declaration is a design-time contract, not a runtime guarantee.
elements.evidence: deployed and started; declared type observed on the process variable

elements.name: Data Store Reference
elements.reason: #166: a typed process-variable declaration, like a data object, not an annotation. The condition validator counts it as a known variable, so referencing one produces no unset-variable warning. What the store POINTS AT is enriched by M6's trusted data repository; the declaration does not wait on it.
elements.evidence: deployed and started; creates NO runtime process variable (#255 -- re-probed against 8.0.0: a process carrying a dataStoreReference, an ioSpecification dataInput and a dataOutput alongside a dataObject reported exactly one variable, the data object's). It is a design-time declaration: the condition validator counts it as a known variable so a condition naming it is not flagged as a typo.
